rv.q: This world premiere production of Isla is certainly an entertaining charmer presented with a lot of heart...
For now, Isla remains a beautiful theatrical vessel whose shadows are more fully alive than the story they have been summoned to illuminate.
Like Communism, collaboratively devised theater is a noble concept that mostly disappoints in practice (when it doesn’t actively horrify).
Isla has strong components–its magical visual environment and the true lives that inspired it–but they haven’t quite fused into a compelling theatrical whole.
All the artistic elements come together in a wonderful, multifaceted production.

cn.t: Critics admire Isla's inventive puppetry and cultural storytelling about a Cuban family's escape, but several find the 75-minute piece lacks narrative substance beneath its beautiful visual artistry.
